recognize_zh: 視野中央兩顆細胞含深紫黑色、粗大的顆粒，顆粒部分覆蓋細胞核並聚集於一側，形態為正常嗜鹼性球；與 inv(16) AML 的異常嗜酸性球（橘紅色顆粒夾雜大型紫色顆粒）不同，背景還有散落的顆粒與母細胞。
features: Two cells with coarse, dark purple-black granules partly overlying the nucleus and crowded at one pole (basophils)
Granules are uniformly dark without an admixture of orange-red eosinophilic granules
Adjacent cell with blue cytoplasm and coarse dark granules over the nucleus (lower left)
Larger cells with fine chromatin and pale, poorly granular cytoplasm consistent with blasts/monocytoid cells
Background scattered dark granules released from disrupted cells
describe_en: Aspirate smear shows two cells containing coarse, dark purple-black granules that partially obscure the nucleus, morphologically consistent with basophils, together with an additional granulated cell and several larger cells with fine chromatin and pale cytoplasm. The granules are uniformly dark and lack the orange eosinophilic granules that coexist with large basophilic granules in the abnormal eosinophils of inv(16). Released granules are scattered in the background. In this relapsed AML with inv(16), these are normal basophils and should not be counted as abnormal eosinophils.

ddx.dx: Abnormal eosinophils of AML with inv(16)
ddx.vs: Show a mixture of orange eosinophilic granules with large, irregular purple-violet proeosinophilic granules, mostly in immature eosinophils with unsegmented nuclei.
Are larger with round central nucleus and densely packed cytoplasm-filling granules, often spindle-shaped, rather than granules overlying a lobated nucleus.
Consists of fine dark azurophilic granules evenly distributed in pink cytoplasm of segmented neutrophils, not coarse granules obscuring the nucleus.
